lastCompletedStory.title: Accept and require oracle forms at filing time on the derived and fast-track paths

nextStoryContext: createLocalIssueOnMain (src/commands/issue-file.ts) now runs a new validateSpecGuardrail (calling the EXISTING validateSpec from src/issues/spec.ts) whenever specSource is present (both --fast-track and --derived-from), before applyFastTrackGuardrails. A missing or invalid spec returns { ok: false, reason: 'guardrail-failed' } before any mutation, same as the other 4 guardrails. spec threads verbatim: index.ts's FileLocalStdinPayload.spec -> _buildCreateIssueOpts -> CreateLocalIssueOnMainOptions.spec -> writeIssueFile's WriteIssueFileOptions.spec -> buildIssueEntry, which now persists it into the written IssueEntry (src/issues/alloc.ts) instead of omitting the key. This closes the gap US-001 (isPlannable's acceptanceCriteria gate, ADR-0051) opened: a freshly-filed --derived-from/--fast-track issue is now immediately isPlannable, with no separate cam spec step required. cam suggestions promote is UNCHANGED (writeIssueFile with no specSource -> stage:idea, guardrail never runs); do not special-case it in production code, only pin it with tests. Any future caller of createLocalIssueOnMain/writeIssueFile with specSource set MUST also supply a valid spec ({ acceptanceCriteria: string[] (non-empty), scope: string (non-empty), gotchas: string[], domainTerms: string[] }) or filing will be refused.

officialDocsValidated.summary: The fetched docs page claims Bun.spawnSync has NO stdin option ('use Bun.spawn to incrementally write to the subprocess's input stream'), which conflicts with node_modules/bun-types/bun.d.ts (SpawnSyncOptions extends BaseOptions, which declares stdin?: In, In extends Writable including ArrayBufferView). Per the 'comment/doc does not prove runtime behavior' lesson, verified empirically instead of trusting either source: `bun -e` on the installed Bun 1.3.13 ran `Bun.spawnSync(['cat'], { stdin: new TextEncoder().encode('hello-stdin-body\n'), stdout: 'pipe' })` and it correctly echoed the piped input (exitCode 0, stdout matched). The new integration test (test/integration/issue-file-spec-channel.test.ts) also exercises this same stdin option against the real `bun index.ts issue --file-local` subprocess and passed. Implementation is therefore aligned with the REAL, current Bun 1.3.13 API; the fetched docs page is stale/inaccurate for this version, not the code.
